item.title: AltTabProjects 1.0.9 — Friends beta
item.description:
# AltTabProjects 1.0.9 — Desktop destinations stay available
Desktop labels remain available in Command-Tab after switching to another Desktop, including when the shortcut shows windows from visible Desktops only. Your monitor filter and ordinary window exclusions still apply.
Labels on other Desktops are discovered without visiting each Desktop first. Creating a Desktop no longer leaves existing Desktop destinations missing from the switcher.
Update through Settings → General → Check for updates now…, or run `brew update` followed by `brew upgrade --cask --greedy horner/projects/alttab-projects`. Version 1.0.5 and earlier require a manual download or Homebrew upgrade before built-in updates become available.
Existing Projects, preferences, permissions and the app's signing identity are retained. Intel and older-macOS runtime testing remain outstanding.

item.title: AltTabProjects 1.0.8 — Friends beta
item.description:
## Fixes
- In **Project for This Desktop**, entering an existing open Project’s name under **Create a New Project** now reuses that Project instead of showing “Choose a different project name.” Its name, identity, windows, folder, and history are preserved. If it belongs to another Desktop, its assignment transfers just as it does when selected from the dropdown. - The Project dropdown now sorts alphabetically by Project name, with natural number ordering and Desktop numbers shown beside the appropriate Projects.
Names are matched using the same case, accent, width, and punctuation normalization as Project folders. Archived and deleted Project names remain reserved; reopen archived Projects through the Project Attic.
## Upgrade
Update from AltTabProjects Settings, download and replace the existing app, or run `brew update` followed by `brew upgrade --cask --greedy horner/projects/alttab-projects`. Existing Projects and preferences are retained.

item.title: AltTabProjects 1.0.7 — Friends beta
item.description:
# AltTabProjects 1.0.7 — Quieter window notifications
Opening or restoring a window on its Project's current Desktop no longer shows an assignment toast.
When a restored window belongs to a Project on another Desktop, the notification offers “Move to Project’s Desktop”. Moving is optional and keeps you on your current Desktop. The action rechecks the window and its destination before moving it; resolved or changed conflicts are discarded. Windows matching several Projects still offer a membership choice.
Update through Settings → General → Check for updates now…, or run `brew update` followed by `brew upgrade --cask --greedy horner/projects/alttab-projects`. Version 1.0.5 and earlier require a manual download or Homebrew upgrade before built-in updates become available.
Existing Projects, preferences, permissions and the app's signing identity are retained. Intel and older-macOS runtime testing remain outstanding.

item.title: AltTabProjects 1.0.6 — Friends beta
item.description:
# AltTabProjects 1.0.6 — Automatic updates
AltTabProjects can now check for friends-beta updates in the background and download, install and relaunch through its built-in updater. New installations check daily and ask before installing. Settings → General lets you check immediately or choose manual checks, automatic checks or automatic installation; existing saved choices are retained.
Version 1.0.5 and earlier need one manual download or Homebrew upgrade to this version before built-in updates become available. Homebrew users can run `brew update` followed by `brew upgrade --cask --greedy horner/projects/alttab-projects` for that first upgrade. Later updates can use the built-in updater.
Existing manual update policies remain manual. Choose “Check for updates periodically” in Settings → General to enable daily checks, or use “Check for updates now…” at any time.
Desktop navigation ignores stale windows whose application no longer has a valid process, so they cannot block switching to a populated Desktop.
The local signed upgrade test retained saved Projects, checked settings and existing macOS permissions. The app keeps its established signing and bundle identity. Activated-license, Intel and older-macOS runtime testing remain outstanding.
